land.text: Southern Rhodesia: 'Rhodesia was the de facto successor to the self-governing colony of Southern Rhodesia'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria draws Southern Rhodesia inside its 'British East Africa' shape (1961-1968); the british-east-africa dossier records the loss to rhodesia at November 1965. The UK did not recognise the declaration: 'the British government continued referring to the country as Southern Rhodesia'.

land.text: the whole state under its new name: 'The country's name was changed to Zimbabwe Rhodesia'

successors.note: 1 June 1979, when Abel Muzorewa became the first black prime minister. Same territory (Cliopatria's two shapes are both 392,765 km2).

capitals.name: Salisbury (Harare)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital and largest city: Salisbury'. Coordinates are modern Harare from the gazetteer (Natural Earth). The page records no change of capital.

correction.text: Southern Rhodesia within its colonial frontiers (modern Zimbabwe), unchanged from the 1967 shape; the declaration of independence of 11 November 1965 changed the government, not the frontier

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Rhodesia row begins in 1967 but the page dates the declaration to 11 November 1965. The land is drawn inside Cliopatria's British East Africa shape until 1968, so the 1967-1968 overlap is for the british-east-africa dossier to resolve.

392,428 km2 for 1967-1975 against the infobox 'Total: 390,580 km2' (ratio 1.00). Gazetteer: 1,310 cells against 1,304 for modern Zimbabwe. The page describes no change of frontier in 1965-1979, so the shape stands.

392,765 km2 for 1976-1978, 0.1% above the 1967 shape; the page records no border change, so this is shape refinement. The page notes that Mozambique became independent in 1975 ('After the Carnation Revolution and the end of Portuguese rule in Mozambique in 1975') but says nothing of a frontier move.

correction.text: the Rhodesia shape unchanged for January to May 1979; the name changed to Zimbabwe Rhodesia on 1 June 1979 (Cliopatria's Zimbabwe Rhodesia row, same 392,765 km2, begins 1979)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria ends its Rhodesia row in 1978 although the state kept the name Rhodesia until June 1979. The rendering must switch from this dossier to zimbabwe-rhodesia at the month, not at the year.

ledger.note: 11 November 1965: Southern Rhodesia's government declares independence from the United Kingdom without British consent. The page: the state 'issued a unilateral declaration of independence (UDI) from the United Kingdom on 11 November 1965'; 'The new nation, renamed Rhodesia, initially sought recognition'. Unrecognised; the British government kept calling it Southern Rhodesia.

2 March 1970: Rhodesia declares itself a republic. The page: 'Rhodesia declared itself a republic on 2 March 1970' and the state was 'officially the Republic of Rhodesia from 1970 onwards'. No territory changes; colour continues.

region.text: the whole state, renamed Zimbabwe Rhodesia

ledger.note: 1 June 1979: Rhodesia becomes Zimbabwe Rhodesia under Bishop Muzorewa. The page: Abel Muzorewa 'became the country's first black prime minister on 1 June 1979. The country's name was changed to Zimbabwe Rhodesia.' The month is the prime minister sentence's; the page does not tie the rename to the day. Bush War page: 'Under the agreement of March 1978, the country was renamed'. No land changes hands.

wars.name: Rhodesian Bush War
wars.outcome: Lancaster House Agreement: 'Military stalemate; ZANU/ZAPU political victory'; 'Rhodesia renamed; Zimbabwe gains internationally recognised independence'. 'On 21 December 1979, a cease-fire was announced.'
wars.note: Infobox span '4 July 1964 - 12 December 1979'; the text gives the cease-fire as 21 December 1979. Raids across the frontier took no ground and are not contest zones: Operation Dingo, November 1977, 'guerrilla camps at Chimoio and Tembue in Mozambique'; 'the ZIPRA guerrilla base at Westlands farm near Lusaka in October 1978'; April 1979, a raid on Joshua Nkomo's residence in Lusaka (Rhodesia page). Mozambique became independent 'on 25 June 1975', adding '1,300 kilometres (800 mi) of hostile border'. Span clamped by the reviewer to the state's life (the war itself began 4 July 1964, before the declaration of 11 November 1965).

certainty.note: The frontier is the Southern Rhodesian colonial frontier, which no page opened records as changing between 1965 and 1979; the war's cross-border raids moved no line. No treaty page was opened for the frontier itself.

notes: Cliopatria rows: 'Rhodesia' runs 1967-1978 but the state was declared on 11 November 1965 and kept the name until 1 June 1979, so the dossier adds keyframes for 1965-1966 and January-May 1979; 'Zimbabwe Rhodesia' (1979-1982, zimbabwe-rhodesia) is the same land under the next name and is written by another group (its found event is also 1 June 1979). Cliopatria's British East Africa shape (1961-1968) still covers Southern Rhodesia in 1967-1968. Rulers omitted: the page lists heads of state from 1970 (Dupont 1970-75; Everard acting 1975-76; Wrathall 1976-78; Everard acting 1978; Pithey acting 1978-79; Everard acting 1979) and Ian Smith as prime minister, but gives 'Field was succeeded by Ian Smith' in 1964 against an infobox '1965-1979', and nothing for 1965-1970 (the governor and officer administering the government), so no complete list was read. The page gives Lancaster House only as 'late 1979' and the end of UDI ('Rhodesia temporarily reverted to the status of a British colony') undated; the zimbabwe-rhodesia dossier carries December 1979. Page budget: two pages. native_names left empty: no page read gives one.
